DIS.rationale: Disney presents a mildly attractive fundamental picture with improving trajectory. The company's Q2 FY2026 results showed 6.5% YoY revenue growth to $25.17B, though EPS declined 29.8% YoY to $1.27 (partly due to higher taxes and lumpy comparisons). The balance sheet is solid with $115.3B equity and improving cash generation ($6.91B operating cash flow in Q2). Streaming has turned profitable with operating income up 88% to $582M in Q2 FY2026, and the Experiences segment remains the profit engine at $2.6B operating income. Valuation is attractive vs. own history: P/E of 14.1x sits near the low end of its 12.5-23.8x range over the past year, and P/B of 1.51x is at the bottom of its 1.5-2.1x range. The stock trades at $98.05, down from a 52-week high of $124.69. Near-term catalysts include Q3 earnings on August 5 with Bank of America projecting improving park attendance and EPS of $1.87, plus the company reaffirming double-digit adjusted EPS growth guidance for FY2026-2027. Risks include FCC regulatory scrutiny on ABC licenses, linear TV decline, and rising sports rights costs, but these are partially priced in at current valuations.
key_factors: Streaming profitability inflection: operating income up 88% YoY to $582M in Q2 FY2026, margin crossing 10% for first time
Valuation near multi-year lows: P/E 14.1x (vs. 12-month range 12.5-23.8x), P/B 1.51x (vs. range 1.5-2.1x)
Experiences segment remains profit engine: $2.6B operating income in Q2, record $10B in FY2025
Q3 earnings catalyst on August 5 with improving park attendance expected per Bank of America
FCC regulatory risk on ABC broadcast licenses and $50M antitrust settlement on carriage fees
Linear TV structural decline partially offset by ESPN standalone service and streaming growth
Management focus on disciplined capital allocation and consistent earnings compounding per CFO comments

sources_cited.excerpt: Streaming operating income rose 88% to $582M in fiscal Q2 2026; SVOD margin crossed 10% for the first time. Record $10.0B Experiences operating income in fiscal 2025.
Bank of America reiterated its 'Buy' rating on Disney shares and a price target of $125, citing expected growth in streaming profitability, a recovery in parks attendance

FCC is actively investigating Disney-owned ABC on two fronts, including political equal-time violations and accelerated license renewal review. Disney agreed to a proposed $50 million class-action settlement over anticompetitive carriage agreements.

Hugh Johnston, CFO, expressed confidence in the company's long-term growth trajectory and emphasized management's focus on disciplined capital allocation and generating attractive returns on invested capital
